content.comment_body: Hello, I am searching for an affordable way to count shaft revolutions. Currently, I use a [product_name] controller on my machine. The supply voltage is 230V AC, and the required frequency or RPM is 500 Hz. I also have a variable speed drive to adjust the motor speed, which prevents using a timer since speed varies based on the rated frequency. My function block program uses a counter driven by the input block. The best approach I’ve considered so far is a proximity switch, but those that switch fast enough operate on DC voltage. If a DC proximity switch could work, how should I connect it to serve as a switch for the input block? Any guidance would be appreciated.

Hi, A frequency of 500Hz is too high for a 230V version of the [product_name] controller, regardless of the voltage the proximity switch handles. Only DC-powered versions can count frequencies up to 5kHz. Please refer to the technical documentation in the [document] for more specific details. [url] Hope this helps.

Thanks. I thought that since the [product_name] software indicated inputs 1 through 4 could switch quickly, my controller supported it as well. That clarifies things. Still, it is essential for me to count the motor’s revolutions, as it’s crucial to the process. Are there any inexpensive alternatives I should consider? My knowledge of available electronic technologies is limited, so I’d appreciate recommendations.

In that case, use the [product_name] DC version—12/24V or 24V DC. It’s inexpensive and performs very well. You can easily configure it for your process, and input switches connect directly to the [product_name] controller.
Is it possible to use a 24V AC/DC expansion module with a 230V AC/DC logic module from [product_name]?

analysis.insight_summary: Participants identified a restriction in the frequency counting capability of a specific [product_name] controller model. The user needed high-frequency input handling (500 Hz), but the 230V model could not support this requirement; only DC-powered models were suitable. The thread illustrates confusion caused by differing product specifications and assumptions regarding 'fast switching inputs.' Users also emphasized a preference for affordable, straightforward solutions.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that the [product_name] controller should accommodate high-frequency counting on digital inputs regardless of version, based on both hardware and software references to 'fast switching.' They are seeking an inexpensive and simple solution to reliably measure shaft revolutions for their application.
